title: Second line and the grand marshal's tricks with brass bands
summary: De De describes how the grand marshal faked turns to fool the second line, which walked and danced.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You talked about the second line, remember?
Mm-hmm, yeah, yeah, yeah.
I was describing it to you. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. The way it used to be.
Well, you see.
How did the second line act when you were playing with those brass bands?
Well, it was the same thing. I don't think I had no chance.
I imagine they do the same thing.
People were more wasted then.
You think so? People were more wasted then, but now they didn't come down.
You know, the grand marshal used to trick them and all like that.
Oh, that's true. I don't know if they'd do that yet. See the grand marshal was parading and he'd get you to the corner like that.
I think they got nine.
Yeah, they was wasting years now.
Dick Allen?
Mm-hmm.
The parade would be going, the grand marshal would be in lead, you know?
Yeah.

And the band behind quite nicely in the regular line up. And the second line would be on one side of the bank and on the other, you know? My grand marshal would stand in the middle street and it'd make like he was going to turn this way. Yeah. Now you see, now if the second line was on that side of the bank, they'd all rush to get on that side to turn that way. Then he'd turn this way all of them. You see? He'd have all of them. He'd be fun at that time, you know? Oh, the second line would be a dog out. He'd run into each other. Yeah. Yeah. He'd make a motion like he's turning this way to turn the corner that way. And all the second line, I'd run ahead, you know? He'd cross on that side of the bank and he'd just turn around and lead the band this way. That's what's up. The car was going in a way. That's what we used to do it.
Well how did they get around? Did they always walk or did they ride bicycles? Walk, walk, walk.
No, no, walk, walk, walk, walk. On the feet.
I see them riding, let's see, the day I saw them on bicycles, roller skates. Everything, everything.
No, no, no. Now I guess today they do it. They do it. I'm walking. They're walking. Women like them in too.
Oh yes.
Dancing in the streets. Oh, same. Oh, same.
Oh, there'll be some time in the day. I saw when she was really shaking today. Oh man. Old woman about 70 years old and she was out there shaking just like she was a kid again.
